name: Product and Fashion Mockups
title: Product and Fashion Mockups
answer: Product and fashion mockups use AI image generation to create photorealistic previews of clothing, accessories, packaging, and other goods without a physical photo shoot. The goal is to show how a product looks on a model, in a setting, or with different colors and materials, often for e-commerce, design review, or advertising. This sits within photography and hyper-realism because the output is judged against the standards of a professional studio photograph.

sections.body: Product and fashion mockups use AI image generation to create photorealistic previews of clothing, accessories, packaging, and other goods without a physical photo shoot. The goal is to show how a product looks on a model, in a setting, or with different colors and materials, often for e-commerce, design review, or advertising. This sits within photography and hyper-realism because the output is judged against the standards of a professional studio photograph.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on diffusion-based image generation models that have been fine-tuned on large sets of product and fashion photography. These models are typically served through cloud GPU instances or local workstations with high-memory graphics cards. Some pipelines combine a base image model with specialized adapters for pose, depth, or segmentation to keep the product geometry stable.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A common workflow starts with a text prompt describing the product and scene, then uses an input image of the product or garment to guide the output through image-to-image or inpainting. Designers often mask the product area and regenerate the background, or keep the background and swap the product texture. For fashion, virtual try-on methods map a garment image onto a person's pose using keypoint or dense pose estimation, then refine the result for fabric drape and lighting.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on who owns the generated image, whether the product design or brand logo is protected, and whether a model's likeness has been cleared. Generated mockups can mislead buyers if they do not match the real product, and some jurisdictions require labeling of synthetic media. Provenance tools that record the model and prompt are becoming standard practice, but they do not resolve underlying copyright or trademark disputes.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward real-time mockup generation inside design and e-commerce tools, where a product image can be placed into many scenes with consistent lighting and perspective. Video mockups and 3D-consistent views are the next step, allowing a single product file to generate rotating or worn-in-motion previews. As control over fabric physics and material response improves, the gap between generated and photographed fashion will narrow.
